home.subtitle: AI-powered testing assistant for your repositories. Follow the steps below to get started.
home.step1Desc: An organization groups your projects and team members. Start by creating one.
home.step2Desc: Connect a Git repository (GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket) to monitor and test.
home.step3Desc: Set up automated test pipelines with AI-powered checks for your project.
home.tip1: Organization switcher is at the bottom of the left sidebar. Use it to switch between organizations.
home.tip2: Projects are linked to Git repositories. Each project can have multiple test pipelines.
home.tip3: Pipelines define automated test checks. Click on a project to create and manage its pipelines.
home.tip4: Notifications can be configured in Settings to alert you about test results via email or Slack.

organizations.noOrgsDesc: An organization is your workspace. It groups projects, team members, and settings together. Create one to get started with AI-powered testing.

orgSettings.title: Settings
orgSettings.subtitle: Manage your organization settings.
orgSettings.deleteDesc: Permanently delete this organization. This action cannot be undone.
orgSettings.integrationsDesc: Connect your Git providers so AI features can access your repositories.
orgSettings.providerTokenPlaceholder: ghp_... or glpat-... or your token
orgSettings.tokenHint: Create a Personal Access Token with repo read/write permissions.
orgSettings.githubHint1: 1. Go to GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens
orgSettings.githubHint3: 3. Select the repositories you want to grant access to
orgSettings.githubHint4: 4. Under "Repository permissions", set Contents to "Read and write" and Pull requests to "Read and write"
orgSettings.githubHint5: 5. Click "Generate token" and paste it here
orgSettings.gitlabHint1: 1. Go to GitLab → Settings → Access Tokens
orgSettings.gitlabHint4: 4. Set an expiration date and click "Create personal access token"
orgSettings.gitlabHint5: 5. Copy the token and paste it here
orgSettings.bitbucketHint1: 1. Go to Bitbucket → Personal settings → App passwords
orgSettings.bitbucketHint3: 3. Select permissions: Repositories (Read, Write), Pull requests (Read, Write)
orgSettings.bitbucketHint4: 4. Click "Create" and paste the password here

projects.noProjectsDesc: A project links to a Git repository (GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket). Once connected, you can set up test pipelines and run AI-powered checks on your code.

pipelines.noPipelinesDesc: A pipeline defines a series of automated test steps that run on your code. You can trigger pipelines manually, on a schedule (cron), or via webhooks on push/PR events.

testWizard.title: AI Test Generator
testWizard.analyzeDesc: Connect to your repository and analyze its structure, test framework, and existing tests.
testWizard.analyzeInfo: The AI will scan your repository to understand the project structure, identify the programming language, test framework, and existing test patterns. This information is used to generate relevant and idiomatic tests.
testWizard.analyzingDesc: Scanning repository structure, config files, and existing tests...
testWizard.proposeDesc: The AI will analyze your source code and propose which tests to create. Optionally specify a focus area.
testWizard.focusAreaPlaceholder: e.g., 'Focus on the auth module' or 'Prioritize error handling in API endpoints'
testWizard.generatingTestsDesc: AI is generating test code for {count} approved item(s)...
testWizard.stepLlmReview: AI is reviewing and fixing the code...
testWizard.validationFailed: Some issues remain after {maxAttempts} attempts. Please review manually.
testWizard.reviewDesc: Review the generated test files. You can edit them before committing.
testWizard.smartGeneratorDesc: Analyze your project, get AI test proposals, review and commit — all in one flow.
